estimand: expected number of non-bot stars a repository receives in the next hour given its recent star history (self-excitation of attention, which mixes contagion with outside referrals)
population: public GitHub repositories with recent stars

selection.rule: E4: among candidates with compute <= 100 us/row, order by the validation primary metric (ties within 1e-4 to the simpler); keep the first unless its validation long-horizon measure is worse than the smallest one with a paired cluster-bootstrap 95% interval of the difference entirely above 0; keep a simple baseline instead if it is strictly better on test
selection.reason: selected on validation and confirmed on test: no simple baseline is better

rule_comparison.mapping: no comparable simulator rule: the social engine's diffusion is share -> inbox -> open of content items and is not defined on repository endorsements; the persistence rule B0 is the rule-based baseline

identification_note: Observational: the dependence of next-hour stars on recent stars mixes contagion, referral bursts and recommender (trending) feedback; it is a reduced-form self-excitation, not a causal diffusion effect.
extrapolation_limits: GH Archive public GitHub events, 2024-10-07..10 UTC: hourly non-bot stars of repositories that received a star in the previous 24 hours. The simulator may use this model for the next-hour arrival rate of endorsements (stars, saves, upvotes) of an item given its own recent endorsement history and activity, i.e. self-exciting attention dynamics on a platform with a trending surface. It may NOT infer: (1) why attention arrives (observational: contagion through followers, outside referrals from news sites and GitHub's own trending page are not separated); (2) cascades of other content kinds or platforms; (3) horizons beyond a day or the long-term popularity of an item; (4) the effect of promotion; (5) items with no endorsement in the last 24 hours (outside the units). Weekday data only.
